title: Integrality from a schematically dense integral open
statement:
Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $j:V\hookrightarrow Z$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], where quasi-compact means that the inverse image of every affine open is quasi-compact. Suppose $V$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and is scheme-theoretically dense in $Z$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], meaning that $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $V$ [def-sc-generic-point], and put $K=\mathcal O_{V,\eta}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $Z$ is integral, $K$ is a field, and for every nonempty affine open $W\subseteq Z$, the intersection $W\cap V$ is nonempty and the restriction followed by the germ map
$$\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Z)\longrightarrow\Gamma(W\cap V,\mathcal O_V)\longrightarrow K$$
is injective.

source.place: Tag 01RE (lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense), the affine restriction-injectivity argument; Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), integral case. This agent-formulated consequence isolates the dense-open/function-field argument in the returned proof, step 2.

proof.text: Since $V$ is integral it is nonempty. Choose a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq V$ (schemes have affine open neighbourhoods). Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to $V$, its given generic point $\eta$, and $U$: it states in particular that $K=\mathcal O_{V,\eta}$ is a field. The open immersion also shows that $Z$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, integral case; affine fraction-field specialization in lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$. By the injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], evaluation on $W$ gives an injective restriction $r_W:A\to\Gamma(W\cap V,\mathcal O_V)$. Explicitly, if two sections have the same image, their germs have the same image at every point of $W$; injectivity of the sheaf morphism makes the germs equal, and the sheaf locality axiom makes the sections equal. If $W\cap V$ were empty its section ring would have $0=1$, so injectivity would force $0=1$ in $A$. But $W$ has a point, hence $A$ has a proper prime ideal by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], impossible when $0=1$. Thus $W\cap V$ is nonempty. This is the affine restriction argument of Stacks Tag 01RE, written out rather than using an additional density lemma.

source.place: Tag 01RE, lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense, and the paragraph immediately before example-scheme-theretically-dense-not-dense

proof.text: The nonempty open $W\cap V$ contains $\eta$: otherwise its closed complement in $V$ would contain $\eta$ and therefore its closure $\overline{\{\eta\}}=V$, contradicting nonemptiness [def-sc-generic-point]. Apply clause 1 of [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] to the integral scheme $V$, its open $W\cap V$, and the point $\eta$ of $V$. Its hypothesis is integrality of $V$, established by the assumptions, and not integrality of $Z$, which is still to be proved. It gives an injective germ map $g_W:\Gamma(W\cap V,\mathcal O_V)\to\mathcal O_{V,\eta}=K$; the lemma has no affineness assumption on this open. Hence $g_Wr_W$ is injective: equality of two composite images first implies equality under $r_W$ by injectivity of $g_W$, and then equality of the original sections by step 2. This is exactly the composite in the statement.

source.place: Properties Section 01OJ, Definition 01OK and Lemma 01ON, and Morphisms Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), integral case; the precise germ-injectivity input is clause 1 of lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/FunctionField.lean:55).

proof.text: For each such $W$, write $\varphi_W=g_Wr_W:A\hookrightarrow K$. Since this is a unital ring map to a field, injectivity gives $1\ne0$ in $A$. If $ab=0$, then $\varphi_W(a)\varphi_W(b)=0$ in $K$, so one factor is zero; injectivity gives $a=0$ or $b=0$. Therefore $A$ is an integral domain. Step 1 gives $Z\ne\emptyset$, and this argument applies to every nonempty affine open of $Z$. These are exactly the conditions defining an integral scheme in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Thus $Z$ is integral; steps 1--3 already give every other asserted clause.
